oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Les perspectives professionnelles des enseignant·es-chercheur·es en début de carrière au prisme du genre
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The under-representation of women in the upper echelons of the higher education hierarchy appears in several international surveys. This article looks at the entry into the profession of teacher-researchers in French universities to determine whether this vertical inequality corresponds to individual decisions made over time or, on the contrary, taken in the first few years. The interviews we conducted revealed a whole range of obstacles that make it more difficult for women to achieve career advancement. The results of the questionnaire used in this study show differences in career prospects leading women, from the very first years, to invest more than men in teaching, to the detriment of research, and to postpone obtaining the habilitation to direct research, which is required to apply for the status of university professor.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: L’approche intersectionnelle en formation : entre tensions, réflexivité et changement professionnel
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The social relations of sex, class and race, “consubstantial and coextensive” (Kergoat, 2009, p. 112) enter the school, influencing the student’s confrontation with learning. With the aim of transforming teachers' representations of learning contexts and developing skills to implement teaching that takes social relationships into consideration, training in the intersectional approach in PE (15 hours) was implemented. place with trainee primary school teachers from the Créteil academy (N=65). The analysis of their conceptions and practices is part of the clinical activity (Clot, 2001). This article will focus on describing the training, its objectives and its limits, then analyze the resistance and sociological issues in the appropriation of the intersectional approach in training.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Pour une approche praxéologique de l’intersectionnalité en éducation et formation(Volume 2)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Education, as a social and political field, is shaped by power relations that are constructed and articulated through multiple social systems of categorization: gender, race, class, disability, religion, and geographic origin. In the face of persistent inequalities and the plurality of educational experiences, intersectionality has emerged as an essential theoretical and methodological framework. Rooted in the foundational work of Black feminism, this paradigm makes it possible to move beyond isolated categorical analyses and understand the mechanisms of domination and marginalisation in their interdependence. This volume provides a critical overview of the uses of intersectionality in educational research and highlights studies that are actively exploring its practical application.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Retisser l'intersectionnalité dans l'histoire de l'éducation des filles au Congo colonial : le cas du Foyer Social d'Élisabethville (1934-1960)
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In history of education, particularly with regard to colonial and women's education, the use of intersectionality as a method of analysing historical sources is growing rapidly. This study contributes to this body of research by (a) exploring how intersectionality can be operationalised in the history of education and by (b) illustrating its application in the specific case of girls' and women's education at the Elisabethville’s (Lubumbashi, DRC) Foyer Social during the Belgian Congo era (1934–1959). More specifically, following Danièle Kergoat's work, it seeks to demonstrate the consubstantiality and coextensiveness of relations of gender, race, class and age domination, to be retraced through the colonial archives of this educational institution for Congolese women and girls.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Analyser l’intersectionnalité par la méthode quantitative : profils de jeunes face à la cyberhaine
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article offers a critical reflection on the methodological implications of applying quantitative methods within intersectional research. It draws on the findings of a doctoral research examining the experiences of adolescent girls exposed to and/or victimized by cyberhate, in comparison with those of boys living in France. By adopting an intercategorical approach, the study explores heterogeneous profiles while considering a broad range of sociodemographic variables, including sex, age, parents’ socio-occupational category, ancestry, and vulnerability status. The findings indicate that belonging simultaneously to multiple minority groups is associated with a significantly higher risk of exposure to and victimization by cyberhate. The article seeks to move beyond the tendency to confine intersectional studies to qualitative approaches, highlighting the relevance and robustness of quantitative methods for advancing this field of research. It also provides recommendations to address the methodological challenges encountered in applying this approach.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: L’intersectionnalité pour repenser sa posture de recherche
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: By initiating numerous reflections related to my own journey, intersectionality has led me to question my position and seek consistency between my status as a researcher and my desire to act for greater social justice. This article is the result of this self-reflective process, which takes the form of an autoethnographic investigation. In it, I analyze my educational background from an intersectional and interdisciplinary perspective, highlighting the elements that have led me to adopt a research stance ethically situated against the reproduction and legitimization of social domination.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Prendre en compte les rapports sociaux dans l’analyse de l’activité de travail des Accompagnant·es d’Elèves en Situation de Handicap
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article is the result of a research-intervention project in educational sciences aimed at analyzing the work activity of the support staff for students with disabilities (AESH, from the French acronym). The request made by the collective involved in this research guided the analysis toward social relations at work that produce a position of inferiority within the organization of schoolwork. As a result, the support staff experiences situations of exclusion within their workplace, whether in informal, semi-formal, or formal settings. However, their identity, particularly gender identity, also constitutes a resource for their work activity. The researcher therefore proposes a re-reading of the transcripts through the lens of gender, race, class, or disability to show that the decisions made by these workers are shaped by social relations. This article argues for the integration of an intersectional approach to complement the field of work analysis to better understand the social relations structuring the activity of education professionals.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La propriété immobilière face aux temporalités des marchés et de ses acteurs
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: While sociology has contributed to empirical studies on how interpersonal relationships shape economic action and how intermediaries guide consumer decisions, little attention has been paid to the temporalities of the capitalist regime and the temporal dispositions of actors empirically. During the 20th century, buying a house became one of the materialized milestones of the “American dream”, at the heart of the motivations and economic actions undertaken on real estate markets. Based on lines of inquiry from the sociology of market activity and economic sociology and an ethnographic survey conducted among real estate agents in a medium-sized city in the American Southwest, this article proposes to question the forms of temporalities at work in real estate ownership, work and transactions carried out by real estate agents. Combining theoretical considerations on the social and economic temporalities at work in real estate markets and field observations on how temporalities act, within a local real estate market, the article explores the conditions of emergence and the temporalities of the imposition of the ideology of real estate ownership, focuses on the temporalities of entrepreneurship among real estate agents, and analyses how tensions are exerted in the temporalities of transactions.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: “They shall not pass!”: British Anti-fascists and the Politics of Violence
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In the 1970s, British anti-fascists resorted to force to prevent the National Front from operating in public. In the 1980s and 1990s, similar tactics were used against the British National Party. This violence was politically motivated and was the latest episode in a long history of militant anti-fascism. It bore only superficial similarities with other forms of mass disorder such as football hooliganism. From 2009, British anti-fascists had to face a new adversary in the form of the English Defence League (EDL), created by extreme right-wing activists and football hooligans. Despite the provocative nature of the EDL’s activities, anti-fascists did not mount a serious campaign of violent opposition. This can be explained by the evolution of the far left, the specificities of the EDL, changes in the labour movement, as well as more repressive policing.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Online Journeying within the Pitt Rivers Cook-Voyage Collections
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Travel was one of the means by which objects were amassed and, if viewed from afar, in space and time, these artefacts may be considered as discursive repositories, other than textual, which compile narratives of journeys. Investigating the mechanics of mediation of these objects (as for text and image) may then be understood as research work in the field of Travel Studies. Artefacts in ethnographic collections have been the object of decolonizing attention and scholarship which challenge for example static, exhibitive on-site praxes. I will thus approach what I will consider as the connected triptych of Travel Studies, “cargo” and the decolonial turn within the framework of a case-study, using the online presentation of the Cook-Voyage Collection at the Pitt Rivers Museum (Oxford) (PRM) as an entry point. The focus will be on specifically digital showcasing, not of exhibitions but of catalogues of online collections /databases of ethnographic objects, which in the absence of decolonial enquiry and action, may well continue to generate elliptical, partial or fragmented experiences of virtual journeying.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: “If It Means Lives Lost That is How it Must Be”: The Ethics of Strike Action in the NHS, from the Winter of Discontent to the Nurses’ Strike of 2022-2023
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Ethical questions are seldom asked about trade union activities and of trade unionists themselves. Both scholars of labour history and industrial relations and trade unionists themselves would regard the altering of the balance of forces with the employers and the state as the key political question in relation to collective action. Still, there exists an area of trade union activism and scholarly interest where one finds a body of literature discussing the place of ethics in collective action, namely in health service unionism and in research on collective action taken by health service workers. This article first discusses the foregrounding of ethical concern as a key discursive device in anti-union, anti-strike coverage of industrial disputes in the UK National Health Service. It then looks at how the development of health service trade unionism in the 1970s was conceived, by trade unionists and scholars alike, as a move away, a liberation from ethical concern, in a mirror image of the anti-strike discourses. Finally, the article looks at the embedded ethics of strike action during the 2022-2023 UK nurses’ strike.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: George Orwell and the Spirit of Protest
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article examines George Orwell’s lifelong cultivation of what is termed the ‘spirit of protest’, a commitment to individual heterodoxy, truth‑telling, and resistance to political orthodoxy. Drawing on Orwell’s essays, fiction, diaries, and political activities, it traces his scepticism toward collective protest movements and his preference for dissent expressed through individual judgement and literary integrity. The discussion situates Orwell alongside writers such as Koestler, Zamyatin, and Camus, highlighting a shared belief in the necessity of perpetual protest against ideological conformity. The article argues that Orwell conceived protest primarily as a writerly vocation, rooted in linguistic clarity and moral honesty, and that Nineteen Eighty‑Four functions as a warning about the annihilation of this spirit through repression, surveillance, historical erasure, and manufactured conformity. Ultimately, it contends that Orwell’s work champions the preservation of heterodoxy as essential to resisting totalitarian tendencies and sustaining the possibility of a free future.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: The Periodical The Examiner’s Coverage of the Crimean War in 1854 and the Problems of the Concept of Progress
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The weekly periodical The Examiner is well-known by name to historians of Victorian Britain but no serious attempts appear ever to have been made to investigate its precise profile over its approximately eighty-year publication run or to identify exactly what justifies its habitual qualification as ‘progressive’ or ‘radical’ or whether such ‘progressivism’ or ‘radicalism’ implied different, fluctuating values as the nineteenth century wore on. Famously, the periodical was where Alfred Tennyson chose to publish his Charge of the Light Brigade, itself an ambiguous reflection on aristocratic military ‘blundering’ during the Battle of Balaclava (1854), and the Crimean War of 1853-1856 offers itself up as rich case study material revealing markers of the Examiner’s purported progressive values and their evolution over time. After establishing a reasonably solid understanding of the nature and profile of the periodical’s editorial staff, this article draws on extensive, and hitherto largely under-investigated, primary source material both from key historical moments before the Crimean War and from key moments during the siege of Sevastopol. It will be shown that the aura of revolt associated with The Examiner in its fiery inaugural years had faded by the time of the Crimean War, partly because of historical change, but also partly because of the innate ambiguities of the concept of progress and its complex relationship to bourgeois goals and ideology.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: “The Interests of All Exploited People Are the Same”: An Analysis of Orwell’s Socialist Perspective
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: George Orwell’s satires, Animal Farm (1945) and 1984 (1949), stand as two of the most iconic political satires of the twentieth century century. They offer forceful expressions of how revolutions are betrayed by the corrupting effects of power, ultimately resulting in regimes more repressive than those they replaced. Yet what began as an internal critique of Socialism was soon recast as an argument against revolution and Socialism. Since his untimely death in 1949, the Left has decried Orwell’s betrayal of its cause, while the Right has appropriated his anti-totalitarian rhetoric in its war against Communism. By situating Orwell’s political and moral thought within its historical context — the turbulent decades of the 1930s and 1940s, marked by capitalism’s deepest crisis, the rise of Fascism and Soviet Communism, and the Second World War — this article seeks to reexamine Orwell’s political thought in the context of the political crises of the first half of the twentieth century, and to reconsider his work in a new light.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: George Cruikshank (1792-1878) in Protest: The Artist as a “Public Moralist”
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: George Cruikshank (1792-1878) was a British illustrator and satirist who used not only his art as a form of protest, but also other forms of communication, such as pamphlets, letters to the press, and oration. Cruikshank’s diverse causes include political lampoons which critique government attempts to suppress this very form of protest, social reforms, and a zealous, almost dogmatic, involvement with the Temperance movement. Taking into account the diversity of the objects and forms of Cruikshank’s protest, this paper will seek to explore the ethical and ideological motivations which led him to engage in public debate, the evolution of his ideas, and his place in a wider ideological context. Examining his expressed desire to impact government or individual actions, we will argue that the many forms of his protest contribute to establish the artist as a Victorian public moralist.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: The Liberal Radicalism of T.H. Green and Edward Caird
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article gives a new perspective on the relationship between liberalism, class and protest in the late-Victorian and Edwardian political thought and activism. It focuses particularly on two leading British idealists, Thomas Hill Green (1836-82) and Edward Caird (1835-1908). Section one introduces the topic. Section two argues against a wide-spread scholarly interpretation of the British idealists as moralising middle-class collectivists. Section three argues that Green was a radical who foregrounded the experiences of the working classes in his practical activism. Section four argues much the same for Edward Caird, relying on his understudied lectures on social ethics. The article concludes that this analysis demonstrates that socially-embedded liberalism can ground a theory of radical class-sensitive politics. Throughout, the article uses a range of sources including previously obscure newspaper reports in local newspapers.

oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The aims of this study were to: (1) provide an overview of the implementation of assessments in mathematics learning carried out by mathematics teachers at MAN 2 Bone during the covid-19 pandemic, (2) find out the obstacles and obstacles for MAN 2 Bone teachers in carrying out mathematics assessments during the pandemic. covid-19 The research method used is descriptive analysis with quantitative and qualitative approaches. The results showed that the implementation of the assessment carried out by MAN 2 Bone teachers in learning mathematics during the pandemic period was quite well implemented. Even so, there are still teachers who experience problems in carrying out math assessments during the COVID-19 pandemic, starting from the difficulty of assessing students' conceptual understanding of mathematics to the decision to determine the final grade of the semester during the COVID-19 pandemic.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Conceptualisations du genre dans les discours de savoirs linguistiques
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In this article, I explore how various linguistic discourses conceptualise gender. By focusing on matters of reference and the extra-linguistic dimension, we can understand which sex/gender conceptions are at play in the linguistic analyses, and therefore how linguistics carries, reproduces or challenges various views on gender (such as natural or as a social order, etc.). More broadly, these analyses provide insights into how grammatical analyses conceptualise the extra-linguistic world to which language refers or that language designates.Using the notion of anti-essentialism as a benchmark, I first focus on 20th-century structuralism, then on the field of typology, and finally on the feminist linguistics from the 1990s. I also discuss some classifications of the various kinds of « genders » existing in Gender & Language Studies.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Dis/continuité référentielle dans les fabliaux médiévaux : variation de genre, points de vue et chaînes anaphoriques
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The comic effect of certain medieval fabliaux is based on the act of cross-dressing: the hero of the story, thanks to a perfectly successful disguise, manages to pass as a person of the opposite sex. However, this doubling of identity is only accessible for certain points of view. From the narrator’s perspective, male and female identities are merely two faces of a single human referent; but for other characters in the story, they are two distinct referents. This raises the issue of referential continuity: a single referent develops multiple anaphoric chains, the nature of which is determined by the point of view applied. In our article, we first analyse the structure of the anaphoric chains associated with cross-dressed referents, highlighting the constraints related to coreferential continuity. Then, we examine the predicates linked to these cross-dressed referents, paying particular attention to the isotopy conflicts induced by the act of cross-dressing. Through a detailed textual analysis of the fabliaux Trubert, Berangier au lonc Cul, and La Saineresse, we address the relationship between gender (a linguistic category), sex (a biological category), and the cultural representation of sex (isotopies).

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La question du référent évolutif à la croisée de problématiques linguistiques et philosophiques. Le cas du « morceau de cire » de Descartes
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This contribution focuses on anaphoric expressions referring to entities that undergo transformations throughout discourse, thereby raising the issue of coreference. It seeks to explore how the notion of an evolving referent gives rise to complex problems that go beyond linguistics, particularly within logical and philosophical traditions. The study will examine how Descartes illustrates this issue through the example of the “piece of wax” in his Meditations: despite the wax’s physical transformations, its identity persists, requiring intellectual rather than sensory recognition. The question of the evolving referent will be addressed within the framework of the philosophy of knowledge, highlighting the role of language in perception and error.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Points de vue textuels et logiques sur les sortes et les changements de genre…
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: We will first remind the origins of linguistic research on evolving referents, at the crossroads of phenomenology and narratology, referential semantics, and textual linguistics. We will move from linguistic to extra-linguistic domains, particularly ontology or metaphysics, because these disciplines raise the (old) question of the relationship between words and the world. Today, the question of how we view evolutionary phenomena is central, and this allows us to work above all on the corpora, (i) in terms of conceptualizations, universes, or images, as far as cognition or our mental representations of the world are concerned, and (ii) in terms of textual dynamics, as far as language is concerned. The diversity of the phenomena and corpora dealt with allows for a diffracted approach to the question of genre insofar as gender evolutions or changes, whether real or fictional, can be transformations that are not only gendered, both within and outside the species, but also conditioned by the genres (types) of texts —according to the conditions imposed by the physics of the world, the phenotype of species, and the way we look at them.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Les variations de genre dans les références aux animaux en anglais : des emplois standards à l’usage militant
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This paper considers the use of gender, more specifically the choice of an “animate” pronoun (he / she) or the neuter, in references to animals in contemporary English. The gender of English, which is semantic and less highly grammaticalised than that of French or German for instance, reflects the speaker’s point of view, with a system based both on ontology and on an “upgrading” principle. As such, it provides precious insights into the relationship between grammar and conceptualisation of the world. The aim of this paper is twofold. First, it seeks to understand how gender variation works. It proposes a brief contrastive perspective with French to achieve that. Secondly, it seeks to understand the linguistic effects of the recent “pronoun activism” that advocates rejecting it in references to animals, as a move against their objectification.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Cross-dimensional cultural identity: a multi-dimensional empirical investigation of VTuber audience behavior through the lens of theory of planned behavior
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: IntroductionThis study employs the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) to investigate the key factors influencing audience intention to watch Virtual YouTubers (VTubers). Guided by the decomposition logic of the decomposed theory of planned behavior, twelve antecedent variables were systematically integrated to decompose the three core TPB dimensions—attitude, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control—within VTuber consumption contexts. Among these, three domain-specific variables—virtual identity identification, ACG culture identity, and cross-cultural influence—were introduced to capture the unique cultural and psychological characteristics of VTuber audiences.MethodsData were collected through an online survey platform, yielding 352 valid responses, and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM).ResultsThe findings reveal that audience attitude and subjective norms significantly and positively influence watching intention, while perceived behavioral control exhibits a relatively weaker effect. Content professionalism and sense of virtual community emerge as the primary antecedents affecting attitude and subjective norms, indicating that audiences prioritize content quality and community connections over virtual identity identification. Time availability proves to be the most crucial determinant of perceived behavioral control, reflecting the constraints of attention economy on VTuber viewing behavior.DiscussionThis study represents the first systematic application of DTPB in quantitative empirical research within the VTuber domain. Beyond contextual application, the findings reveal important boundary conditions: the unexpectedly weak effect of virtual identity identification challenges prevailing assumptions about avatar-based consumption, while the dominance of time constraints over economic barriers provides empirical evidence for attention economy dynamics in virtual entertainment contexts. The results offer both theoretical insights into TPB’s applicability boundaries in emerging virtual content domains and practical implications for platform operation and content design strategies.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Insegurança alimentar das famílias rurais do Semiárido nordestino brasileiro, seus determinantes e impactos dos programas do FIDA
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Despite decades of rural development interventions aimed at strengthening family farming, improvements in productive capacities do not always translate into better food security conditions. This article examines this gap in Brazil’s Northeastern semi-arid region through the analysis of six projects funded by the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD). Using a longitudinal dataset of more than 9,000 rural households observed between 2017 and 2022, the study evaluates changes in a synthetic food insecurity index that captures constraints on both the quantity and diversity of food consumption. The results do not indicate a statistically significant average effect of the projects on food insecurity. Instead, food insecurity remains consistently associated with structural factors such as income, education, and basic household infrastructure. These findings suggest the need to better integrate productive initiatives with broader social protection policies and improvements in material living conditions in rural areas.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Diferente, desigual, desconectada? Paradoxos da alimentação contemporânea no mundo urbanizado e num regime agroalimentar de base industrial
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article examines the relationships between urban food practices and the processes of multiculturalism, hybridity, and globalization. Drawing on the theories of Stuart Hall and Néstor García Canclini, it discusses how the dynamics of difference, inequality, and connection manifest themselves in contemporary food. It analyzes urban commensality as a hybrid practice, marked by the standardization of diets, the commodification of diversity, and the deterritorialization of food. It highlights how technological advancement and globalization intensify inequalities and the loss of cultural references in food. It concludes that it is essential to rethink urban food practices based on the notions of difference, inequality, and connection to understand the paradoxes of food multiculturalism and imagine counter-hegemonic alternatives to production and consumption.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Três teses sobre a agricultura de plantação
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In this essay I propose three theses on plantation agriculture. I start by arguing that plantation agriculture has intrinsically thanatopolitical purposes and effects, which lead to the proliferation of biological and cultural death. Then, expanding Emmanuel Levinas’ philosophy beyond the human, I propose that plantation agriculture is inherently immoral because it denies the face of the other, both that of the damned of the Earth and that of non-humans. I conclude by suggesting that the problems created by plantation agriculture can only be solved by refusing the hierarchical way of ordering the world that the plantation illustrates, which can only happen if the world – including agrarian relations – is reorganized according to anarchist principles.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Democracia alimentar e governação em rede: reflexões a partir da experiência da Comunidade dos Países de Língua Portuguesa
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This paper examines how transnational networks of actors can strengthen food democracy in contexts marked by strong power asymmetries. Drawing on a framework that combines network governance, social participation, and rights-based approaches, it analyses two case studies within the Community of Portuguese-Speaking Countries (CPLP): the Civil Society Network for Food and Nutrition Security and the UNESCO Biosphere Reserves Network in the CPLP. Using primary data, participant observation, and institutional process analysis, the paper explores the potential and limitations of these networks in creating more inclusive decision-making spaces, institutionalising participatory mechanisms, and promoting sustainable, sustainable food system models. The findings show that, despite financial and institutional constraints, these networks influence public policy, strengthen collective action, and contribute to multi-level governance arrangements. The essay concludes that transforming food system governance requires sustained social mobilisation and institutional commitment.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: « De la bonne et de la mauvaise littérature »
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This interview provides insights into Gilles Carpentier’s career in the literary world. This little-known figure in the literary world is of interest because it played an essential role in the development of so-called « Francophone » literature between 1979 and 2003, at the Seuil publishing house, as the editor of Ahmadou Kourouma and Sony Labou Tansi, among others. Gilles Carpentier is also the author of six novels which, though forgotten today, bear witness to a rich relationship with literature. Through the intertwining of these two strands of his life’s journey, his partner, Claude Thomas, and his son, Mathieu Carpentier, present who he was and what he did as a literary éminence grise.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Représentations du français du Québec et du français de France au Brésil
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Recently, the ties between Quebec and South America have strengthened. There is an increasing demand for French as a Foreign Language (FFL) courses focused on Quebec-spoken French, particularly in Brazil. However, there is little research on this variety in the field of FFL in this country. In this context, we designed a study aimed at analyzing the representations of Quebec French in Brazil. To do this, we conducted interviews with twenty participants, including ten teachers and ten learners. The interviews covered their learning and teaching experiences, their contact with the French language, as well as their perceptions of French from Quebec and French from France. The results show that participants have a positive view of diatopic variation. Negative representations are few, but French from Quebec remains less valued than French from France. The former is often associated with a formal register, while the latter is often seen as synonymous with the standard norm.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Le passeport de prise de risques linguistiques : regard critique sur un dispositif d’entrée en littéracie universitaire pour les étudiant·e·s en situation d’exil
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Learning a language in a context of exile goes beyond linguistic proficiency; it also involves autonomy, academic resilience, and adaptation to an unfamiliar university culture. An analysis of university support programs designed for students in exile highlights shared priorities and makes it possible to develop an analytical framework used to examine the linguistic risk‑taking passport. Used at the University of Ottawa, this tool encourages learners to experiment with the language in context, to accept mistakes, and to build confidence and autonomy while strengthening their oral skills. This study analyzes the passport’s written tasks based on competencies associated with academic literacy, including reproduction, reformulation, and the ability to connect knowledge. The results show that while some activities foster creativity and personal expression, few enable mastery of academic conventions. The integration of targeted, progressive, and contextualized exercises, as well as the pedagogical use of AI, could strengthen structuring, argumentation, and synthesis, providing refugee students with comprehensive support to succeed in their academic journey.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La diplomatie langagière des Moose ou la résilience devant la mort par les formules de salutations
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In their daily expressions, the Moose use linguistic detours to convey a message or to express their moods. This allusive language is remarkable in a situation of mourning where information on the death as well as greetings are coded, on purpose, in order to respond to social ethics. The present reflection, which questions the language mechanisms of the Moose as well as the effects sought in the choice of a detailed lexicon in the context of mourning, is based on a corpus of greetings used in the same circumstance. The ethnolinguistic analysis of the corpus revealed that the Moose have a post-mortem philosophy of life on earth. This conception makes death a phenomenon, certainly, irreversible but gratifying in that it allows access to the happiness where the ancestors are supposed to be. Also, the greetings participate in a dynamic of sublimation of death in order to make it less devastating. Death is, therefore, compared to trivial realities or socially rewarding elements.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Littératie de l’IA et stratégies rédactionnelles en français langue seconde à l’université : quelles spécificités pour les étudiant·e·s en exil ?
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This paper looks at artificial intelligence (AI) literacy and writing strategies in French as a second language (FSL) among university students in exile in French-speaking Belgium. The study, conducted in the framework of a preparatory French course for university studies at UCLouvain, assesses students’ behaviours in generative AI‑assisted writing. It compares their practices with those of students trained in the local learning culture. The authors examine the digital practices of migrant students in their daily and academic lives, and the impact of AI on FSL writing. The results do not support the hypothesis of an AI literacy profile proper to students in exile and suggest they should not be treated differently from other foreign language learners. The study nevertheless highlights some migrant-specific digital behaviours and allows for the formulation of pedagogical recommendations to foster AI literacy applied to foreign language writing among university students in exile.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Stance in Contrast: A Corpus-Based Study of English and French Academic Writing
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: While previous research has highlighted the importance of stance in academic writing, cross-linguistic research on academic stance remains limited and often focuses on a narrow set of features, offering only a partial view of how writers express evaluative meanings across languages. Using a unified framework, this study examines epistemic and attitudinal markers in two corpora of English and French research articles. Stance markers were identified and disambiguated through a corpus-driven method based on Jadoulle (2023), and their frequencies and lexical preferences were compared. Results show that English writers use stance markers, especially hedges, more frequently than French writers, and that both groups rely on distinct lexical resources to express epistemic and attitudinal meanings. These results suggest that English and French academic writing are shaped by different rhetorical expectations and underscore the need for culturally informed approaches to academic writing pedagogy.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Accompagner le projet d’orientation universitaire des étudiant·e·s en exil via une focalisation sur les genres discursifs
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Following the observation that students in exile in France frequently change their academic direction, the study identifies the difficulties they encounter in developing their career plans, based on interviews with the students and teachers concerned. The analysis highlights needs relating, on the one hand, to a better understanding of training programs and professions and, on the other hand, to the ability of students to identify and promote their aspirations and skills. Teaching approaches are proposed to meet these needs, with the aim of strengthening the support that teachers provide to these students. From a literacy perspective, the aim is to have students work on different discursive genres grouped into three categories (informational, narrative, and academic communication genres) that are considered complementary from a teaching perspective. This complementarity is illustrated through an example in which a specific approach approach) is presented for working on skills assessments (narrative genre category), which is then linked to the task of writing a cover letter (academic communication genre category).

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Accompagner l’intégration des personnes en exil dans un cursus universitaire : le rôle du feedback dans la rédaction de la lettre de motivation
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: As part of the Passerelle degree programme, students in exile receive support in writing a personal statement to pursue higher education in France. This process involves reconciling two requirements: highlighting the uniqueness of the student’s background, while harmonizing the content and form of the letter with the norms of the discourse genre. It involves producing several versions of the text over several months, each generating extensive written feedback from the teacher. Analysis of more than 900 items of feedback highlights the features of this form of written interaction, through a taxonomy of written feedback. The results show that although the majority of feedback focuses on linguistic forms, the initial texts undergo significant transformation in terms of content. The guidance helps to better highlight the background and skills of each student in exile, while bringing the writing closer to the expectations of a personal statement for admission to a university programme in France.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Favoriser l’acculturation aux discours universitaires dans le programme passerelle Horizon académique : la prise de notes comme objet d’enseignement-apprentissage
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This contribution examines the teaching-learning of language skills that enable acculturation to discourses in higher education by students from migrant backgrounds. The Horizon académique bridging programme at the University of Geneva welcomes migrant students with a threefold objective: to prepare them for B2 level of the CEFR, provide them with the tools and resources to pursue higher education and live in Geneva. We begin by presenting the recently developed pedagogical framework, with a focus on notetaking activities. We then analyse how students acquire this skill, using data collected as part of their university course support, which runs alongside their French lessons. Our data show the need to rely more on their multilingual skills. They also highlight the heterogeneity of practices depending on the course of study and the need to better integrate digital tools, while questioning the purpose of notetaking.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Un outil pour la réussite académique des étudiants en exil : réflexions sur l’amélioration d’un portfolio pour l’immersion universitaire
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: In this article, we analyse, with a portfolio, a university immersion programme designed for students in exile. The approach adopted is holistic (like the framework of French for Academic Purposes) and tailored to learners with diverse backgrounds. The Diplôme Universitaire Passerelle at USN, intended for students progressing from B1 to B2 level, combines disciplinary immersion with linguistic support. The portfolio documents listening and reading traces as well as reflective writing, thereby facilitating acculturation to French academic literacy. Academic immersion plays multiple roles in this process of acculturation, while the portfolio, understood as a form of “mediating writing”, enables students to carry out a self-analysis of the difficulties encountered, particularly in navigating transitions between academic cultures. The dual objective is both to support students during their university immersion and to consolidate their experiential knowledge.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Perception des agro-pasteurs et dynamique d'une plante proliférante (Hexasepalum sp.) dans les parcours agro-pastoraux du Sénégal
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Sahelian rangelands, which are essential to agro-pastoral systems, are increasingly degraded by climate change and human pressures. In several agro-pastoral areas of northern Senegal, herders have reported for decades the proliferation of a herbaceous plant belonging to the genus Hexasepalum. This vegetation dynamic raises growing concerns due to its perceived effects on forage availability and quality. In this context, this study aims to analyze agro-pastoralists' perceptions of the emergence, spread, and pastoral impacts of this proliferating plant. Focus group discussions involving over 650 participants were conducted across 13 municipalities in Senegal's agro-silvo-pastoral zone.Results indicate that most people said the plant first appeared to the Doly Ranch in the late 1970s. The surveys highlight a progressive spread of the species across rangelands, mainly through zoochory, along with perceived impacts on subsistence activities and competition with palatable forage species. The plant is generally considered poorly consumed by cattle, reinforcing concerns about the availability of pastoral resources. Most people say that cows do not like to eat this new plant. This makes it harder for animals to find enough food.These results underline the value of local knowledge in documenting vegetation dynamics in agro-pastoral systems. They also highlight the need for further botanical and ecological research to better characterize this proliferating plant and to inform rangeland management strategies.Translated with DeepL.com (free version)

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: De l’attente des emails de Biden à la crise des déportations de Trump : le peuple haïtien hurle dans la forêt de l’humiliation
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Haitian migration to the United States has been shaped by alternating policies of welcome and repression, reflecting a geopolitical dynamic of control and exclusion. Since the 1990s, political and economic crises in Haiti have driven migrants to seek refuge in the United States. U.S. immigration policies have fluctuated between temporary protections and mass deportations, often leaving Haitian migrants in precarious situations. This study examines how Haiti's structural dependence on the United States shapes its migration patterns and socio-economic vulnerabilities. Under Trump, the end of Temporary Protected Status and increased deportations reinforced the marginalization of Haitians. Under Biden, despite promises of leniency, restrictive measures persist. The Haitian diaspora plays a crucial role in supporting Haiti's economy through remittances. The article argues that current U.S. policies exacerbate Haiti's socio-political instability and reinforce its economic dependence. Haiti must adopt a proactive strategy to leverage the potential of its diaspora and diversify its international partnerships.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La géophagie (njang pemba) chez les Ndjuka-Kotika de Guyane et du Suriname, étude ethnographique
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The consumption of white clay (njang pemba) among the Maroons of French Guiana is a practice well known by the medical professionals and the local population, but poorly understood in its cultural complexity, and widely controversial until now. Through 54 interviews conducted with Maroons women and men (mostly Ndjuka-Kotika) between Cayenne, Saint-Laurent du Maroni and Paramaribo, we tried to better understand the origin, the production, the perceptions and the place of this practice and of the pemba object as well as their contemporary evolution. Mostly produced in Suriname, where they are made as part of family activities, the balls are then clandestinely exported to French Guiana. Essentially feminine, often associated with pregnancy, the oral consumption of pemba seems to be inseparable from other, external practices, closely associated with the spirits (Obia) of the ancestors. A vector between the living and the spirits for some, a protection for others, white clay is much more than a simple pica, and the public health actors who mobilize around it cannot ignore the cultural importance of this substance.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Les implications de la fiscalité locale sur l'environnement économique et sur le schéma institutionnel et statutaire à envisager dans le cas de la Guadeloupe
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Several studies have analyzed in the past the significant impact of tax policy on economic growth, on environmental protection and on job creation in countries with a worrying financial and economic situation. In this context, the objective of this work is to determine, in the case of Guadeloupe, the optimal tax rate that maximizes economic growth, favors investment, encourages job creation and reduces negative environmental externalities. In doing so, this study provides guidelines, and a reading grid to the elected representatives of Guadeloupe, engaged today in a lively debate on the institutional future of this territory. An error correction model, and in addition, the Armey model (1995) were used for this purpose, with data covering the period 1995-2023. The results obtained reveal that the optimal taxation rate of Guadeloupe today amounts to 7% of GDP against an average effective rate of 11% over the analyzed period. They also show that when the overall tax rate increases in Guadeloupe by 1%, economic growth decreases in this territory, by 0.6%. Finally, the significant difference observed between the optimal tax rate and the average effective rate, has the consequence of inducing significant perverse effects in the economy. Therefore, the resulting low economic performance invites the authorities of Guadeloupe to undertake without delay profound reforms in tax, economic and institutional matters in order to correct the main disturbances thus created. In conclusion, we recommend that the authorities of this Department proceed to the establishment of a less recessive tax system, with a targeted advantage, less disproportionate, and more democratic, as part of new relations with France.

Over the last few decades, several tourist projects aiming to rehabilitate derelict farms have been carried out and have resulted in a novel type of tourism referred to as “farm tourism” or “agritourism”. Tracing back the history of agricultural heritage is of paramount importance to understand the characteristics of this tourist activity. That is why; this paper will deal with colonial farms and mainly earlier projects on the conversion of decrepit colonial settlements.This study will also shed light on the significant role that colonial heritage plays in the development and promotion of tourism in Tunisia. In fact, it is thanks to tourism that reconciliation with this type of heritage can be reached. Colonial tourism, which was previously ostracized, currently contributes to create and guarantee authentic and sustainable cultural tourism.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: L’évolution démographique à Haïti : tendances passées et perspectives d’avenir
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article analyzed Haiti’s demographic evolution over the past few decades to better understand socio-demographic changes and nuance the idea of a homogeneous population. The study used a descriptive approach based on the analysis of demographic indicators from several data sources: National Institute of Statistics of Haiti, IPUMS International, World Bank, United Nations (World Population Prospects), and Demographic and Health Surveys. The results indicated that Haiti’s population has grown from approximately 500,000 in 1804 to nearly 12 million in 2024. This growth has been accompanied by rapid urbanization, a decrease in average household size, and an increase in female-headed households. Fertility is declining but remains above the replacement of generations, while the population remains very young. Additionally, international migration is significant, with more than 1.7 million Haitians living abroad. Progress in mortality has also been exceptionally rapid, with life expectancy at birth increasing significantly. While analysis of these indicators provides a better understanding of demographic trends in Haiti, it requires a degree of caution. The reliability of the indicators obviously depends on the quality of the data used.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Paisaje social y género en el Caribe continental. El caso de la “educación” de las mujeres mayas en la península de Yucatán a partir de Diego de Landa
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article analyzes the Relación de las cosas de Yucatán by Fray Diego de Landa as a colonial device for legitimizing the exploitation of Mayan women and the peninsular territory during the sixteenth century. Based on four methodological axes — temporality and sources, spatiality, scale and instrumentalization of education — it is examined how the Franciscan friar built a social landscape that equates the Yucatecan territory with the Mayan female bodies, attributing to both qualities of resistance, fertility and productive utility within the encomienda system. It is argued that the colonial chronicles, far from offering direct access to the indigenous feminine world, reflect the logics of power that produced them. Education - understood as evangelization - operated as an instrument of ideological subjection that stripped Mayan women of their agency and reduced their textile know-how to an economic input susceptible of being exploitable. It is concluded that, although colonial sources are valid historiographical tools, they are insufficient and even dangerous to understand the experience of contemporary Mayan women without a rigorous critical analysis.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: The Model of Aruba’s International Action: The Kingdom as a Vehicle
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: While, for many years, we are witnessing an increase in the involvement of sub-state entities on the international stage, this article displays the case of Aruba, one of the non-independent territories of the Caribbean, a region often left out by the literature in this field. Despite the predominance of States, sub-states entities enjoy variable freedom in matters of international affairs. In this regard, each entity shapes its own model of practicing international action. These models lay on several variables: the links between the territories’ international action and the foreign policy of their respective States, the beliefs of territorial and State actors, the logic of coordination and consultation with the central power and the coexistence between territorial actors and State actors. Based on these factors, this paper draws the lines of the model of Aruba’s international action. It contributes to reveal the relationship Aruba is maintaining in the international field with its State, the Kingdom of the Netherlands. It shows that despite benefiting a large autonomy in its internal affairs, Aruba choses to drive its international action through the Kingdom’s apparatus, that it judges necessary.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Formations et emplois en temps de crise : entre attentes et perceptions. Le cas du secteur du tourisme au Maroc
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: Crises, whether health, economic, political, or environmental, have a direct impact on the tourism sector, which in turn has a significant impact on vocational training in this field. The Covid-19 pandemic is a perfect example of the negative repercussions, both on the tourism sector and on the academic and professional careers of students in hospitality and tourism. The latter, in particular, find themselves facing a double challenge: on the one hand, the need to adapt to a changing job market, and on the other, the questioning of their initial choice of training. For these students, the process of planning for their professional future becomes a major concern. This article uses the case of Morocco to analyze the impact of the health crisis on the career paths of tourism students and the influence of perceptions of careers in the tourism and hospitality industry, examining the mechanisms of risk perception and adaptation strategies. Using a multidisciplinary approach, we seek to understand how these crises are changing the representations, motivations, and trajectories of a generation that is set to become one of the pillars of the tourism recovery.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Analyse Spatiale de l’évolution du trait de côte de la Baie d’Ain el Turk (Oran, Algérie) à l'aide des techniques géospatiales
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The western coast of Oran, which is characterized by varied morphological units, constitutes a particularly interesting area for the study and understanding of the natural and anthropogenic influence on its dynamics. Galloping population growth, the increase in economic and tourist activities and also, growing urbanization have led in recent years to modifications of the natural space and also to a degradation of the environment of certain beaches on this coast. This work proposes an approach that combines GIS and remote sensing at all levels and is based on the measurement of the coastline evolution of the beaches of the bay of Ain El Türck using both multi-temporal resolution satellite data (TM and OLI) and the geographic information system (GIS) for the period of the last 31 years, from 1985 to 2023. From statistical analyses based on the variations of the coastline, calculated from the two EPR and LRR methods of the DSAS system, the study of coastal dynamics showed on the one hand, a generalized retreat and thinning of the beaches reaching in some places around twenty meters per year in the sectors of Cap Falcon and Ain El Turck between 1985 and 2016 and on the other hand, a clear accretion in this sector in 2023. This study demonstrates that the combined use of satellite imagery and statistical methods such as regression for shoreline change analysis is useful for erosion monitoring and preventive measures.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Le principe du droit à la scolarisation universelle : repères, enjeux et limites dans le contexte haïtien
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article examines the right to education and the obstacles to its realization in Haiti. Many children, particularly street children, are invisible within the educational system (François, 2009). Although education can reduce the risk of conflict by 20% per year and promote peace, several barriers to universal schooling exist. Approximately 617 million children worldwide have not acquired minimum skills in reading and mathematics (UIS, 2017), and over 85 million children aged 6 to 15 affected by conflicts are not enrolled in school (UCW, 2025). In Haiti, inequalities, extreme poverty, lack of resources, privatization of education, and insufficient international cooperation hinder the implementation of universal schooling. The study proposes concrete measures to strengthen school infrastructure, train teachers, and increase international cooperation. Finally, it emphasizes the importance of an inclusive and collaborative approach to overcoming educational challenges and ensuring a better future for Haitian children.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Contourner, disposer, relier, coexister : quelques éléments communicationnels de l’expérience esthétique et politique chez Rancière et Glissant
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: The aim of this article is to reflect on the communicability of the sensory experience of the world based on the relationship as poetry that weaves together times, spaces, bodies, and knowledge in Jacques Rancière and Édouard Glissant. By drawing a possible dialogue between these two authors, we intend to highlight how the relational power of the actions of skirting, arranging, and relating helps us to experience communicational processes of deviation in a different way, with a view to elaborating a “moving constellation” of forces, relationships, and powers that escape the normally visible. Our argument aims to show that it is possible to transform the edge of dispositional operations into a relational margin of maneuver to expand mobilities, to articulate singularities in lacunar spaces of play in which skirting, arranging, and coexisting shape experiences to be communicated, shared, and constantly re-signified in the struggles and insurgencies that aim to respond to the urgencies of forms of life that resist and maintain hope. The sensitive experience that brings together the scene (Rancière) and the archipelago (Glissant) highlights interdependencies, intertwining, and unpredictabilities that make surfaces and contact zones jump and tremble.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Du pouvoir empathique de la littérature. L’examen des violences faites aux femmes dans Pluie et vent sur Télumée Miracle de Simone Schwarz-Bart : vers une renégociation des rapports de pouvoir
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: When a contemporary observer decided to probe the cruel mechanics of domination and narrate the cyclical and unstable dynamics of domestic violence in 1972, this was not the thematic focus that seemed to be the primary focus of critical attention.Winner of the ELLE Readers’ Grand Prize the year following its publication, Simone Schwarz-Bart’s novel "Pluie et vent sur Télumée Miracle" offers an avant-garde exploration of the narrative and reflections on women’s lives, on the conversation between the sexes, and on the mechanisms of inferiorization, the logic of domination, and social reproduction, highlighted in scenes of everyday life. Questioning the avenues for analyzing the politics of emancipation at work in a classic of French literature, it is important to observe what a reflection on fear and courage can offer the reader. The narration of a timeless situation, soluble in the air through trivialization, allows us to grasp a transtemporal movement, one of the best-known histories of violence, those inflicted on women. Literature, a place of self-creation, an ideal place for a founding act, allows us to see and act better. Writing is still about fighting and fertilizing.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: La « doctrine Donroe » à l’épreuve du chavisme. Le pari risqué de la transition au Venezuela
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: By launching the Absolute resolve operation against the regime of Nicolás Maduro on January 3, President Donald Trump wanted to put into practice in Latin America the "Donroe Doctrine", his new conception of international relations based on negotiation imposed by force and coercion. By removing the Chavista leader and his wife, the American president thought that he would find himself in a situation of advantage against a decapitated regime, in the hands of Delcy Rodríguez, a frightened vice president, and a very weakened state apparatus. The words and images of an unusual violence were aimed at disorienting what was left of the regime. But, against all odds, the Chavistas put aside the issue of Nicolás Maduro’s betrayal to focus on the survival of the regime, showing pragmatism before dogmatism. This article analyzes the positions of both enemies, now forced to work together, and wonders about the future in which the Venezuelan opposition, for now outside the transition process, will have to make its way if it wants to wrest power from the heirs of Hugo Chávez.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Ton beau capitaine de Simone Schwartz-Bart, une pièce au diapason de l’effervescence socio-esthétique du champ théâtral caribéen des années 1980
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: When approaching Simone Schwartz-Bart's literary work, it is clear that her theatrical work has been largely overlooked. Published in 1987, Ton beau capitaine remains the Guadeloupean writer's one and only play. Performed in Guadeloupe in April 1987, directed by Haitian Syto Cavé, it premiered at the Festival des Francophonies in Limoges that same year, before disappearing from the stage for several decades. In 2017, director Maud Galet Lalande, director of the theatre company Les heures paniques, staged the play, which toured France (Festival d'Avignon, Metz, etc.), Africa (in the cultural centres of the French Institutes) and the overseas departments (French Guiana, Martinique, Guadeloupe in 2022). The theatrical fate of this play could, at first glance, justify the assumption that Simone Schart-Bart had suffered a setback in her theatrical writing career. However, the Guadeloupean writer's play occupies a very significant place in the history of Caribbean drama. It reveals the state of Caribbean theatre, which, from the mid-1970s onwards, opened up to a renewal of its thematic horizons and dramaturgical modalities, and saw the emergence of a generation of Caribbean playwrights (Maryse Condé, Ina Césaire, Gerty Dambury).

Through the notion of “Haitians from outside,” the article explores logics of belonging, tensions surrounding citizenship, and forms of long-distance nationalism. In doing so, it challenges the classical conception of the Haitian nation-state – grounded in the triptych of territory, borders, and sovereignty – by revealing an alternative, transnational geography constructed by the actors themselves. The diaspora thus becomes a political and symbolic space for the reconfiguration of national identity and the redefinition of relations between Haiti and its dispersed citizens.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: « Carbone bleu » et sédiments profonds dans la ZEE française de La Passion - Clipperton : enjeux de conservation et d’atténuation climatique
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article analyzes the strategic significance of carbon sequestration within the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ) of the La Passion-Clipperton atoll (France). The marine ecosystems, particularly the deep-sea sediments associated with the EEZ's seamounts, constitute a Blue Carbon sink of critical importance for global climate change mitigation. However, current protection (a 12-nautical mile Marine Protected Area) is deemed largely insufficient to counter intensive and illegal overfishing, which threatens the integrity of the trophic chain essential for carbon export to the seabed. The article argues that France must assert its international leadership by integrating marine conservation into its carbon neutrality objectives. The central proposal is the immediate extension of the Marine Protected Area (MPA) to a minimum of 50 nautical miles, supplemented by the establishment of a Managed Marine Area (MMA) over the remainder of the EEZ. This approach, grounded in the law of the sea and the necessity of securing climate assets, represents a concrete and urgent measure for the long-term preservation of marine carbon sinks in the North-Eastern Pacific.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Evaluation of the Adiwiyata Program at Junior High School 23 Palembang
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This study aimed to analyze the evaluation of the Adiwiyata program at State Junior High School 23 Palembang. This type of research is field research carried out in the scene or the place where the symptoms being investigated occur. This research approach uses a qualitative approach. Data collection techniques using observation, interviews, and documentation. The data analysis technique used is data analysis technique according to Miles and Huberman, namely data reduction, data presentation, and verification. Evaluation of the Adiwiyata program at State Junior High School 23 Palembang focused on using the CIPP (Context, Input, Process, Product) evaluation. Supporting factors for the Adiwiyata program at 23 Palembang Junior High School, namely 1) a large schoolyard for planting and gardening; 2) the presence of ornamental plants; 3) availability of water channels; 4) availability of waste bank; 5) greenhouse; 6) the presence of a clean water tank; 7) schoolyard using paving blocks; 8) budget funds from the government for the Adiwiyata program; and 9) school residents work together. The factor that hinders the implementation of the Adiwiyata program at SMPN 23 Palembang is the COVID-19 pandemic, where students cannot participate in the Adiwiyata program activities at their schools. In addition, students lack awareness of the environment, so teachers must provide education and socialization to them about Adiwiyata to create healthy schools that care about the environment.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Writing Against History/Memory
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article links linguistic nationalism and print media by inspecting narratives from four newspapers popular in Assam, a northeast Indian state, at the time when spontaneous mobilizations against the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) 2019 peaked. Drawing from the vernacular and regional press, the article departs from the extant literature on the CAA, that mostly dwells on its constitutionality and legality. The present argument explores the scant studies on vernacular print media in Assam, the interplay between this media and collective memory, and the history of Assamese linguistic nationalism vis-à-vis Bengali. With the political crisis activating “memory frames” that viewed the CAA as an “event,” these narratives went far beyond just demands for repealing the law. The article argues that it rekindled colonial-era narratives of “linguistic domination” by Bengali in Assam and aroused fears, real or exaggerated, of the Assamese language and identity becoming extinct. The print media also reflected historical grievances according to which Assam is a neglected and oppressed state. The article paints a complex picture of the anti-CAA stir in Assam with language at its center harboring deep historical concerns that go beyond the recent political shifts and Hindu/Muslim or citizen/foreigner binaries.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: How teacher–student collaborative assessment relates to L2 writing self-efficacy: insights from Chinese EFL learners
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: ObjectiveTeacher–student collaborative assessment (TSCA) has attracted increasing attention as a participatory assessment approach in L2 writing, yet its relationship with writing self-efficacy remains underexplored, particularly in secondary-level EFL contexts. This study aimed to examine whether TSCA was associated with changes in students’ L2 writing self-efficacy and whether different patterns emerged across gender and internally defined pretest performance subgroups.MethodsA quasi-experimental pretest–posttest design was implemented with two intact Grade 10 classes in a Chinese senior high school. One class received TSCA-based writing instruction, whereas the other followed a traditional teacher-centered assessment approach. Writing self-efficacy was measured using an adapted questionnaire, and supplementary qualitative data were collected through semi-structured interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and t-tests, while interview data were examined through thematic analysis.ResultsThe experimental group showed stronger improvement patterns in overall writing self-efficacy than the control group, including improvement in both task self-efficacy and skill self-efficacy. Within the experimental group, no statistically significant gender difference was observed in the subgroup comparisons, whereas differences were observed across internally defined pretest performance subgroups, with the higher pretest-performing subgroup showing a stronger improvement pattern than the lower pretest-performing subgroup. The interview findings provided supplementary insight into how students perceived the TSCA process and how these perceptions differed across subgroups.ConclusionThe findings suggest that, within the present instructional context, students in the TSCA group showed more favorable patterns of self-efficacy development than those in the comparison group. This pattern was observed in overall writing self-efficacy and in both subdimensions, although subgroup findings were exploratory and should be interpreted cautiously. Given the quasi-experimental design, the single-school sample, and the limited subgroup analyses, the results should be understood as context-bound rather than as strong causal evidence.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Electrochemical Monitoring of Cadmium Stress in Manihot Esculenta Crantz Using Hydrogen Peroxide as a Functional Biomarker
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: An electrochemical method based on differential pulse voltammetry (DPV) employing a glassy carbon electrode was developed for the quantification of H _2 O _2 in Manihot esculenta Crantz cell suspensions derived from tuber explants. Cell cultures were exposed to different concentrations of cadmium (Cd ^2+ ) for 24, 48, and 72 h. The analytical protocol exhibited a limit of detection of 10.28 μmol l ^−1 and a limit of quantification of 51.81 μmol l ^−1 . Cadmium treatment induced a transient increase in H _2 O _2 levels, consistent with an oxidative burst followed by antioxidant-mediated regulation. This behaviour reflects the dynamic activation of redox signalling pathways in cassava cells under metal stress. Overall, the findings indicate that M. esculenta Crantz may serve as a promising sedentary biomarker for cadmium contamination, providing a sensitive, reproducible, and cost-effective strategy for environmental monitoring in tropical regions.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Optimizing catheter-directed thrombolysis access and predicting post-thrombotic syndrome in acute entire-limb DVT: a retrospective cohort study and nomogram development
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: BackgroundSelecting the optimal catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) access for acute entire-limb deep vein thrombosis (DVT) remains controversial. This study aimed to compare the technical and clinical outcomes of three CDT access approaches and to develop a prognostic nomogram for predicting post-thrombotic syndrome (PTS) based on hemodynamic and procedural variables.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed 172 patients with acute entire-limb DVT who underwent CDT via contralateral femoral vein access (CFVA, n = 87), ipsilateral popliteal vein access (IPVA, n = 34), or ipsilateral calf venous access (ICVA, n = 51). Procedural metrics, angiographic patency, and 2-year PTS incidence were evaluated. A LASSO-Cox regression model was utilized to address multicollinearity, identify independent PTS predictors, and construct a prognostic nomogram.ResultsAlthough CFVA afforded the shortest sheath insertion time (1.74 ± 1.02 min), it required significantly longer access establishment (17.07 ± 6.81 min) than IPVA and ICVA (P < 0.001). Antegrade approaches (IPVA and ICVA) yielded superior femoropopliteal thrombus clearance and enhanced inflow patency compared to CFVA (P < 0.001). The 2-year PTS incidence was significantly higher in the CFVA group (59.8%) versus the IPVA (38.2%) and ICVA (41.2%) cohorts (P = 0.033). LASSO-Cox analysis identified poor inflow patency (HR 3.19), poor outflow patency (HR 2.17), and deep femoral vein axial transformation (HR 2.44) as independent risk factors for PTS. Prolonged thrombolysis duration and subsequent endovascular interventions were protective. The developed nomogram demonstrated excellent discriminative ability (C-index = 0.82).ConclusionFor acute entire-limb DVT, antegrade CDT access optimizes early femoropopliteal thrombus resolution. However, long-term PTS prevention is fundamentally driven by comprehensive hemodynamic restoration rather than the initial access site alone. Our proposed nomogram serves as a robust, evidence-based tool for individualized risk stratification and clinical decision-making.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Revisiting the structural and optical properties of γ-N2
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: For decades, γ-N2 has been known to exist at very low temperatures and pressures, located in a tiny area of the nitrogen phase diagram. Recently, it was shown that γ-N2 occupies most of the P–T space usually associated with molecular phases such as δ, ɛ, and ζ, and that it plays a pivotal role in shaping nitrogen’s phase diagram. Using powder synchrotron X-ray diffraction, Raman and infrared spectroscopy, and density function theory calculations, we have investigated the structural and optical properties of γ-N2 in a wide P–T range. The combined X-ray diffraction and infrared spectroscopy results unequivocally demonstrate that γ-N2 adopts the monoclinic (P21/c space group) configuration with two N2 molecules per unit cell. It appears that the γ-N2 is structurally closely related to θ-N2, leading to both phases having very similar Raman signatures. Additionally, the Raman spectroscopy reveals a vibrational mode intensity resonance effect in both phases, caused by a strong vibrational coupling between the isotopic 15N14N and 14N2 vibrational excitations.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Deep learning-based dental age estimation in adolescents using panoramic radiographs: a comparative study with traditional methods
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: IntroductionAccurate dental age estimation is a vital component of forensic identification, orthodontic treatment planning, and medico-legal assessments. Conventional approaches, such as Demirjian's and Cameriere's methods, are limited by observer variability and population dependency. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning (DL) offer potential for objective, reproducible, and scalable assessment through panoramic radiology. This study aimed to develop and validate a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based model for dental age estimation among adolescents using panoramic radiographs and to compare its accuracy with traditional manual methods.MethodsA total of 296 panoramic dental radiographs from adolescents aged 9–19 years were analyzed, with balanced representation across age groups and comparable distribution between male and female participants. Images were divided into training (70%, n = 207), validation (15%, n = 44), and testing (15%, n = 45) subsets. All images were preprocessed, normalized, and augmented prior to model development. A CNN-based regression model was trained using mean squared error as the loss function and evaluated using mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and Pearson correlation coefficient (r). Grad-CAM visualization was employed to enhance interpretability of model predictions.ResultsThe proposed CNN model achieved an MAE of 1.12 years, RMSE of 1.37 years, and a strong correlation (r = 0.96) between predicted and chronological age, outperforming traditional Demirjian and Cameriere methods. Activation maps confirmed that predictions were based on biologically relevant anatomical regions, including developing third molars and mandibular growth zones.ConclusionAI-driven panoramic radiographic analysis provides a robust, interpretable, and ethically compliant framework for adolescent dental age estimation. These findings highlight its translational potential in forensic odontology, pediatric dentistry, and legal age verification, supporting a shift toward standardized, data-driven dental diagnostics.

oai_dc:dc.dc:title: Theoretical and legal assessment of risks associated with public sphere transformation in the era of strong artificial intelligence
oai_dc:dc.dc:description: This article provides a theoretical and legal examination of the risks arising from the transformation of the public sphere under the hypothetical influence of the development of strong artificial intelligence (AI), focusing on specific legal challenges and threats from the introduction of autonomous AI systems into the processes of public administration, law enforcement, and public policy navigation. The study was performed using standard research methods (metaphysical and dialectical methods, analysis, synthesis, systematic investigation, method of abstraction, induction, and deduction) and discipline-specific methods (comparative and formal legal analysis). Some predictions were made about the influence of strong AI on the course of public administration and about the potential technological consequences of using strong AI capabilities at different levels of government and in various areas of human life. Special attention was paid to the issues of responsibility for AI actions and ongoing transformations in the traditional understanding of democratic institutions. The theoretical and legal problems generated by the autonomy and unpredictability of strong AI, which may occur in the field of public administration, were discussed. In general, the findings offer a more profound perspective on new phenomena that arise as a result of human–AI interaction, thus expanding the subject of legal regulation.
